key_insight: Random train/test splits substantially overestimate ML performance for perovskite photovoltaics because many records are duplicated or near-duplicated, so grouped evaluation is needed to measure real generalisation.
engineering_relevance: This provenance-grouped protocol gives researchers a more reliable benchmark for selecting models that can predict new perovskite devices, institutions, and future discoveries rather than memorising known recipes.
method: Mapped institutional provenance in the Perovskite Database.
Built a hierarchy of grouped splits that progressively isolate duplicates, publications, and institutions.
Benchmarked 13 models across the new evaluation regimes and compared feature importance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that nearly two-thirds of curated devices share an exact recipe with another, causing random splits to leak information and inflate performance.
watch_item: Grouped splits are more realistic but may reduce apparent scores and require careful provenance tracking, especially when metadata are incomplete or inconsistent.
paper_title: Provenance-grouped protocol for evaluating machine learning in perovskite photovoltaics
